scope: Review of pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, including its current PAH classification name, transplant referral, and histology.

keyRecommendations.text: PVOD is also called PAH with overt features of venous/capillary involvement.
Early referral to a lung transplant centre is essential because the response to therapy is poor compared with other PAH.
Explants show fibrous veno-occlusive lesions. Immunosuppression is generally not recommended except in systemic diseases such as SLE.

clinicalBottomLine: Treat PVOD as a venous form of pulmonary arterial hypertension that responds poorly to the usual PAH drugs. Refer early for lung transplant.
notableCaveats: Individual case haemodynamics are not generalised as the definition.

source.title: Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease: illustrative cases and literature review.
